canonical_outcome: Price contingent payoffs using no-arbitrage and stochastic discount-factor reasoning.
derivation_review: Finite states all have positive physical probability. Unit-payoff bond price is positive; unrestricted signed real quantities, one horizon and no interim funding, costs or default are explicit. Gross safe R_f and risky G are distinguished from simple R and r_f.

No-arbitrage definition includes negative initial cost and nonnegative terminal payoff; banking initial receipts establishes equivalent zero-cost criterion. Law of one price and linear functional are proved separately from positivity.

Fundamental theorem necessity constructs the residual at a closest simplex point to the zero-cost payoff subspace; compactness, closed finite-dimensional subspace, segment derivative and d_s>=norm(d)^2>0 establish strict positivity before bond normalization. Sufficiency checks positive and zero terminal-payoff cases.

Completeness is payoff-column rank S; uniqueness of q follows from the transpose kernel. Incomplete positive solutions admit q+-epsilon v perturbations. Unique price for a claim iff in traded span follows from its orthogonal residual; unique q does not imply unique holdings with redundant assets.
Sub/superhedge arbitrages and open digital bounds are proved for the exact Aster case; general endpoint claims are qualified. Lab supports changed stock quotes and both lower-subhedge branches.

m=q/pi, E[m]=B, Q=q/B, fundamental pricing and excess-payoff equations have correct units and normalization. Physical belief changes keep q fixed and alter m and expected return, not the no-arbitrage price.

Covariance risk-premium identity and absolute Cauchy bound derived with zero-variance/constant-kernel/equality cases. Attainability distinguished from moment inequality; explicit priced payoff achieves equality only because complete unrestricted market permits its replica.

Consumption Euler equation uses increasing differentiable concave utility and interior two-sided feasible trades; buy-only zero holding gives E[mX]<=p. No aggregate equilibrium, representative investor or empirical consumption calibration claimed.
